actions.name: Target internet-exposed PLCs with malicious project file interactions and data manipulation
actions.description: Iranian-affiliated APT actors targeted internet-connected operational technology devices, including programmable logic controllers (PLCs), causing operational disruption and financial loss by maliciously interacting with project files and manipulating data on HMI and SCADA displays.

actions.name: Download malicious project file to targeted PLC using configuration software
actions.description: At one U.S. victim, the FBI observed the APT actors download a malicious project file to a targeted PLC using configuration software, which retained ladder logic for downstream function but added logic overriding safe operating parameters.

actions.name: Access internet-facing PLCs using leased third-party hosted infrastructure and manufacturers’ PLC programming software
actions.description: Iranian-affiliated APT actors used several foreign-based IP addresses and leased third-party hosted infrastructure along with manufacturers’ PLC programming software to connect to misconfigured victim PLCs.

actions.name: Use Dropbear SSH software on victim modems to gain remote access through port 22
actions.description: The actors utilized Dropbear Secure Shell (SSH) software on victim modems to enable remote access through port 22.

actions.name: Exfiltrate device project files from PLC devices using configuration software to threat-actor-controlled infrastructure
actions.description: Iranian-affiliated APT actors used configuration software such as Rockwell Automation’s Studio 5000 Logix Designer, Schneider Electric’s EcoStruxure Control Expert, and Siemens’ Totally Integrated Automation (TIA) Portal on leased third-party hosted infrastructure to exfiltrate device project files from PLC devices to threat-actor-controlled infrastructure.

actions.name: Modify and delete project file logic including Add-On Instructions and manipulate data on HMI and SCADA displays
actions.description: After extracting device project files, the actors modified and deleted project file logic including Add-On Instructions (AOIs) and manipulated data displayed on HMI and SCADA displays, disabling critical shutdown and alarm logic.

actions.name: Target PLC devices on ports 44818, 2222, 102, 502, and modems on port 22
actions.description: Inbound malicious traffic targeted PLC devices on ports 44818, 2222, 102, and 502, as well as modems on port 22.

relations.rationale: using leased, third-party hosted infrastructure and manufacturers’ PLC programming software to connect to misconfigured victim PLCs enables downloading malicious project files
